3.speaker: Lucian Galade
3.text: "I'll keep working with them and keep you updated, Mr. President."

4.speaker: Player
4.text: "We need to work closely with NFP, they are our only potential partners."

5.speaker: Player
5.text: "And what good does that do to us?"

6.speaker: Petr Vectern
6.text: "We will be ensuring that the Supreme Court can no longer block constitutional changes."

7.speaker: Petr Vectern
7.text: "Most of them won't. But we already talked about a possible agreement with Isabel which may change things. We could potentially get Heron and the Sollist judges as well."

9.speaker: Lucian Galade
9.text: "Most people already find the Supreme Court's absolute authority over constitutional changes dangerous. Look at the situation we currently have, Mr. President. The Judiciary has power over every branch."

10.speaker: Petr Vectern
10.text: "That's why the Old Guard have bargaining chips over us."

11.speaker: Petr Vectern
11.text: "Yes. This will ensure that the Supreme Court will no longer have absolute power over legislation. We can persuade the other parties with this too."

12.speaker: Lucian Galade
12.text: "There are some people in USP who would support a new Constitution with more executive powers. Getting the support of the NFP nationalists is our best bet on this path."

13.speaker: Petr Vectern
13.text: "Yes, we'll need to talk to Judge Edmonds. If we can get to her and Judge Garaci, we might be able to get enough votes. They have major influence."

14.speaker: Player
14.text: "You are part of my cabinet. You wouldn't dare."

15.speaker: Lucian Galade
15.text: "Apart from these two critical points we could address a lot of the issues already in discussion for our own benefit."

16.speaker: Lucian Galade
16.text: "NFP want to reform the appointment procedures of the ministers. Mr. Kibener clarified that the Assembly should have a say in the formation of the council of ministers. They are a potential ally so this is an important demand to consider."

17.speaker: Lucian Galade
17.text: "We could address the term limits and election threshold as well."

18.speaker: Petr Vectern
18.text: "That is something that a majority in our party also supports."

19.speaker: Petr Vectern
19.text: "Well... That one is a controversial one. I doubt that USP would like that."

20.speaker: Lucian Galade
20.text: "Immunity of the Justices, the impeachment of the president, the power of the presidential decrees... All of these are in the realm of possibilities."

21.speaker: Player
21.text: "I disagree. We'll push for comprehensive reforms."

22.speaker: Petr Vectern
22.text: "Well, regardless of what you decide, we will need to work together with all the cabinet to push this agenda."

23.speaker: Lucian Galade
23.text: "I'm with you on this, Mr. President."

24.speaker: Player
24.text: "I agree. Let's keep the changes small and manageable."

25.speaker: Lucian Galade
25.text: "If we can establish a proper balance and get the support of the NFP, you can gain a lot from these changes."

26.speaker: Petr Vectern
26.text: "I'd say keeping everything in the middle ground is the safest bet. No need to agitate anyone too much."

27.speaker: Lucian Galade
27.text: "As long as we accomplish our goals, I also agree."

28.speaker: Nia Morgna
28.text: "What? You were working on a different draft while we worked in the committee?"

29.speaker: Lucian Galade
29.text: "That said, we should try to reach a common ground with the conservative wing of our party to be able to propose such changes in the Assembly."

30.speaker: Player
30.text: "We will do what's necessary to get them in line."

32.speaker: Player
32.text: "They will surely support a just cause for the country and its future."

38.speaker: Narrator
38.text: Nia was taken aback by the statement.

39.speaker: Lucian Galade
39.text: "That is correct. Mr. President had *stronger* ideas. Surely, I couldn't work with the reform committee. No offence."

40.speaker: Player
40.text: "Can we pass it through the Supreme Court?"

41.speaker: Player
41.text: "Can we possibly reach a two-thirds majority in the Assembly?"

42.speaker: Petr Vectern
42.text: "We should reach out to the judges in secret. Some of them might be willing to break rank to support us."

43.speaker: Lucian Galade
43.text: "Now if we are going with this direction, I'll need everybody to focus."

46.speaker: Narrator
46.text: Lucian pulled out a huge dossier from his briefcase.

47.speaker: Nia Morgna
47.text: "I wish you a good day, Mr. President. We'll see what happens in the Assembly and the Court."

48.speaker: Narrator
48.text: She spoke with a gentle tone but her face couldn't hide her disappointment and anger.

49.speaker: Player
49.text: "We need the Court to even pass this change. Why on earth would they support this?"

51.speaker: Player
51.text: "This is already what we wanted to do."

52.speaker: Petr Vectern
52.text: "We will definitely need to work with some of the Old Guard aligned judges."

53.speaker: Player
53.text: "Did you already work on a plan?"

55.speaker: Lucian Galade
55.text: "I'm afraid it would be tough to bribe the Old Guards. Chief Justice Hawker will do their best to undermine us. But maybe we can get to Heron Garaci."

57.speaker: Player
57.text: "We did it before for the elections. We can unite it again."

58.speaker: Lucian Galade
58.text: "We need at least 6 of the 11 judges to vote for the proposal. But Mr. Hawker has enormous influence over the judges."

59.speaker: Lucian Galade
59.text: "According to such change, constitutional amendments will still require the two-thirds vote system to be able to propose a change. However, the judiciary will not have the final say in the amendments."

60.speaker: Petr Vectern
60.text: "This is a point that was unanimously agreed on by all parties. Tarquin Soll established this rule to protect his '29 Constitution. We can break the power of the Old Guards with this."

62.speaker: Lucian Galade
62.text: "I'll move on to the second point then. The new Constitution should remove the Supreme Court out of the constitutional amendment process. Not only popular, it would also strengthen our position against the judiciary."

64.speaker: Petr Vectern
64.text: "That's true. We have bigger fish to catch."

66.speaker: Petr Vectern
66.text: "Oh she will. I don't think she has that in her."

70.speaker: Nia Morgna
70.text: "According to the Constitution, I am a member of the Supreme Court, which means you already have one vote against this. I already know two of the judges who are with me, as well."

71.speaker: Nia Morgna
71.text: "I'm starting to doubt that, Mr. President."

72.speaker: Nia Morgna
72.text: "I can't believe you are all in this."

74.speaker: Lucian Galade
74.text: "While I respect her, I doubt that she's capable of creating major obstacles for us. But we have to keep close eyes on her."

76.speaker: Player
76.text: "Yes, keep an eye on her. We can't let her sabotage us."

77.speaker: Player
77.text: "I'm sure we can work something out with you, Mrs. Morgna."

78.speaker: Player
78.text: "I will make sure she stays in line."

81.speaker: Player
81.text: "Who do you think would be willing to support these changes?"

82.speaker: Nia Morgna
82.text: "I meant no disrespect, Mr. President. But you should be aware of my position, and that it is final."

83.speaker: Narrator
83.text: She left the room and slammed the door behind her.

84.speaker: Player
84.text: "So, we don't even have a vote in the Court?"

86.speaker: Petr Vectern
86.text: "Come now, Mrs. Morgna. You said you were open to discuss Mr. President's version of the new Constitution."

87.speaker: Narrator
87.text: She gave a fake smile and left the room.

89.speaker: Player
89.text: "Do you think they can be persuaded?"

92.speaker: Petr Vectern
92.text: "Well, we don't. I doubt that any of the judges would support such changes just like that. But they can surely be bribed."

93.speaker: Petr Vectern
93.text: "I think we can reach out to Judge Edmonds. And in extension, Mr. Dalton and Mr. Martin. They aren't working together with the Old Guards, as far as we know."

94.speaker: Petr Vectern
94.text: "I know you will. If you can get their support, we'll have enough votes to amend the Constitution, counting we have the support of Mr. Kibener too."

95.speaker: Player
95.text: "Be careful with what you decide to do, Mrs. Morgna."

97.speaker: Player
97.text: "Good day to you too, Mrs. Morgna."

98.speaker: Petr Vectern
98.text: "I'm sure it's possible. But regardless of my opinion, we *need* to persuade most of them to support us for passing an amendment to the Constitution."

100.speaker: Nia Morgna
100.text: "You must be talking about Gloria Tory. She's well respected by the Sollists. She's the biggest problem in our party."

101.speaker: Narrator
101.text: She took her notes and stood up.

102.speaker: Lucian Galade
102.text: "We'll never be able to get PFJP to work with us. But if you can get Kesaro Kibener to work with you on this, our only remaining problem would be uniting our own party."

103.speaker: Lucian Galade
103.text: "We need the majority of our 130 seats in the Assembly to vote in favour. But without NFP's support of 40 votes, we can never surpass the needed 166. Mr. Kibener's full support as well as our party is needed."

104.speaker: Nia Morgna
104.text: "With all due respect, I will take my leave from this meeting. I don't think I have anything to add anymore. I cannot associate with plans of tyranny."

105.speaker: Lucian Galade
105.text: "But it will be tough to unite the USP with all the divisive wings that have formed. You must make them follow you loyally."

106.speaker: Lucian Galade
106.text: "You could technically choose to take no action instead of signing or vetoing it. Without a proper definition of the process, it would be perfectly legal for you to ignore a bill indefinitely."

107.speaker: Nia Morgna
107.text: "A pocket veto? You think that's clever, Mr. Galade but anybody who understands the law would see that hole. There is no way the reformists would be deceived by that."

108.speaker: Lucian Galade
108.text: "They are the biggest obstacle. Even if we pass the Assembly, the Chief Justice will do his best to block our amendments."

110.speaker: Player
110.text: "Let's get into the details of our *reforms.*"

111.speaker: Lucian Galade
111.text: "We have established two points parallel to the demands of the reformists. I'll go through each of them and get your input."

112.speaker: Nia Morgna
112.text: "But judging by what Mr. President is trying to do, I believe you can find common ground under Sollism. The problem will not be her but me, Mr. President."

113.speaker: Petr Vectern
113.text: "And there is one key person who can help us get their support."

114.speaker: Player
114.text: "I like the idea. What kind of loopholes do you have in mind?"

115.speaker: Lucian Galade
115.text: "We can also try to "persuade" the centrists of the Court. I think we might get Mr. Dalton and Mr. Martin with a bribe. The toughest will be Mrs. Edmonds."

116.speaker: Player
116.text: "We could limit the vetoes and package it as a great reform."

118.speaker: Player
118.text: "No. We don't need to change the Article about vetoes."

119.speaker: Petr Vectern
119.text: "And there is another key person who can help us get their support."

120.speaker: Petr Vectern
120.text: "I like the idea. Maybe we could convince some of the reformists with that. But it all depends on the whole changes. It could be better not to change anything."

121.speaker: Petr Vectern
121.text: "We'll need to reach out to Judge Edmonds and her centrist wing. We can get three votes from them. They don't seem to be in the pocket of the Old Guard and they are definitely not reformists."

122.speaker: Petr Vectern
122.text: "I agree. If we're going against the reformists anyway, why even bother giving concessions?"

123.speaker: Nia Morgna
123.text: "Okay then. Let's see what we're talking about here."

124.speaker: Lucian Galade
124.text: "Well, we could define a process for the Assembly to override your vetoes with a supermajority. While this limits your veto capabilities, if we do not define a time limit for the President to act on a bill..."

125.speaker: Petr Vectern
125.text: "Albin Clavin and his reformist wing will be completely against you. He already responded negatively in the committee meetings. But I think he will still be open to discussion."

126.speaker: Petr Vectern
126.text: "We will also need to get more votes from the conservative judges. I believe Heron Garaci might be the weakest link of the Old Guards. He can help us get the 6 votes needed."

127.speaker: Narrator
127.text: She did not even try to respond.

128.speaker: Player
128.text: "Yes, Mrs. Morgna. I am a Sollist."

129.speaker: Lucian Galade
129.text: "Or better yet, we could change the article according to their demands but establish new loopholes for you to hold your veto powers."

133.speaker: Player
133.text: "Come now, Mrs. Morgna. There's no need for that."

134.speaker: Nia Morgna
134.text: "I cannot allow a more authoritarian Constitution to be made. There is no way I can support this."

136.speaker: Petr Vectern
136.text: "However, the conservatives may be persuaded easier. The influence of Soll is still living strong in the party. They might follow you if they respect you as a strong leader."

137.speaker: Lucian Galade
137.text: "We'll start with Section 1. Reformists want your absolute veto power to be removed, or at least, limited. We could potentially give them what they want by limiting it. It wouldn't cause problems since we already have the majority in the Assembly."

139.speaker: Petr Vectern
139.text: "So we need as many of the conservatives to support us. And there is one key person who can help us get their support."

140.speaker: Player
140.text: "But we need more executive powers to bring bigger change."

141.speaker: Nia Morgna
141.text: "I'm sorry, Mr. President but that's the Sollist talking point. I won't be convinced by that argument."

142.speaker: Petr Vectern
142.text: "The conservatives have around 40 seats. If you can get the unaligned to support us, along with our "loyalists" we'll have enough votes."

143.speaker: Nia Morgna
143.text: "Of course, Mr. Vectern. But I already have a strong opinion about what it contains."
